title: India A Face Pakistan Shaheens in Doha on Sunday in Rising Stars Asia Cup
excerpt: Tilak Varma's India A meet the defending champions at West End Park at 3:30 p.m. IST on November 22, with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi against teenage pacer Ali Raza the matchup to watch.
body:
• India A play Pakistan Shaheens on Sunday, November 22 at West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha, starting 3:30 p.m. IST (1:00 p.m. local time).
  • The 50-over Rising Stars Asia Cup runs November 19-29 in Doha with eight teams and 15 matches; Pakistan Shaheens are the defending champions.
  • India A, captained by Tilak Varma with Rinku Singh as vice-captain, open against Nepal on Friday, November 20 before the Pakistan game.
  • Watch in India on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV, in the US and Canada on Willow TV, and in the UAE on Starzplay.

India A and Pakistan Shaheens meet in Doha on Sunday, November 22 in the group match that will draw the biggest audience of the Rising Stars Asia Cup, a 50-over tournament for 'A' and emerging teams that began in Qatar on November 19.

The match is at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium and starts at 3:30 p.m. IST, 1:00 p.m. local time in Doha. It is the second India-Pakistan meeting in the Gulf in a week: last Sunday, India's Under-19 team beat Pakistan off the final ball of the U19 Asia Cup in Oman, chasing down a target of 338 with one wicket in hand, The National reported.

The tournament

The Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026 is being held in Doha from November 19 to 29 across two venues, West End Park and the University of Doha for Science and Technology Cricket Ground. Eight teams play 15 matches in the 50-over format: Group A has Sri Lanka A, Bangladesh A, Afghanistan A and Hong Kong, while Group B has India A, Pakistan Shaheens, Nepal and the UAE. The top two in each group reach the semi-finals on November 26 and 27, with the final on November 29. Pakistan Shaheens, as Pakistan A are known, are the defending champions.

India A begin against Nepal on Friday, November 20, also at West End Park, and finish the group stage against the UAE on Tuesday, November 24.

Players to watch

India A are captained by Tilak Varma, with Rinku Singh as vice-captain, and the squad named in the tournament viewing guide published by Rajasthan Royals includes Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Prabhsimran Singh, Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav. The National picks out Sooryavanshi, the young opener who has already played international cricket this year, as India's leading attraction.

Pakistan's subplot runs through teenage fast bowler Ali Raza, who made his mark in the Pakistan Super League this year and, The National notes, has dismissed Sooryavanshi more than once in age-group cricket — and who had a forgettable U19 final against India on Sunday. Pakistan have also brought back Haider Ali, wicketkeeper Rohail Nazir and pacers Mohammad Hasnain and Akif Javed from the 2019 emerging team.

How to watch

In India, the tournament is on the Sony Sports Network — Sony Sports 1 and 2 in English, Sony Sports 3 in Hindi and Sony Sports 4 in Tamil and Telugu — with live streaming on Sony LIV. In the US and Canada, Willow TV carries the matches. In the UAE, the tournament streams on the Starzplay app, according to The National. In Pakistan, broadcast guides list PTV Sports and the Tamasha app.

What comes after Sunday

Both teams close the group stage on Tuesday, November 24 — India A against the UAE and Pakistan Shaheens against Nepal — before the semi-finals on November 26 and 27 and the final on Sunday, November 29, all in Doha. With only two teams per group advancing, Sunday's result puts the winner in control of Group B.
